title: Pivotal Health - embeddings / reranking discovery
summary: Discovery for embeddings + reranking for Pivotal Health internal search/assistant. They currently use a mix of Elastic + Pinecone for vectors, want to evaluate Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for HIPAA-regulated data. Primary concerns: throughput (100 qps target), latency SLO ~200-300ms, vector dimensionality and storage costs, hybrid search (BM25 + rerank), and audit/KMS for PHI. Agreed to run a benchmark on 100k vectors and to share security docs and pricing. Next call to be a technical demo with benchmarks results.
next_steps: Redwood: send SOC2 + HIPAA security whitepaper and KMS integration notes (Sofia) - due 2026-05-19
Redwood: share Dedicated pricing for 8-GPU reserved pool and Hosted burst options (Sofia) - due 2026-05-18
Redwood/Customer: schedule benchmark run on 100k vectors; provide sample dataset or schema (Rachel) - schedule by 2026-05-20
SE to demo hybrid search (BM25 + vector rerank) with example queries in follow-up meeting (Ethan) - meeting: 2026-05-22
action_items: Sofia Martinez: email security whitepaper and compliance pack; due 2026-05-19
Ethan Cho: prepare benchmark plan (scripts, metrics, expected output); due 2026-05-18
Rachel Lee: share sample vector dataset (anonymized) and top 100 queries; due 2026-05-20
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Sofia from Redwood, AE, with Ethan our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Rachel Lee: Good, thanks. Morning from our side, we're excited to go through this.
[00:12] Tom Watkins: Hey all. Quick scheduling note, we've got about 45 minutes.
[00:16] Sofia Martinez: Great, we'll keep it tight. Quick intros then we'll go into current stack and goals.
[00:23] Ethan Cho: Hi Rachel, Tom, Priya — I'm Ethan, I focus on inference and embeddings at Redwood.
[00:29] Priya Srinivasan: Priya, security. I'll ask the compliance questions.
[00:33] Sofia Martinez: Perfect. To start, can you walk us through the primary search/rerank use case and what success looks like?
[00:40] Rachel Lee: Sure. We power a clinician assistant and an internal knowledge base. Queries can be short or paragraph length. Currently we use Elastic for BM25 and Pinecone for vector similarity; we do a two-step flow — candidate recall from Elastic then vector rerank. Success is relevance improvement over our current baseline and latency under 300ms tail.
[00:56] Sophia Martinez: Thanks. What's dataset size and vector dimensionality?
[00:59] Rachel Lee: Right now ~1.2M docs, about 800k vectors after dedupe. Most embeddings are 1536 dims from an OpenAI model, but some older batches are 768. We're evaluating moving to a single strategy.
[01:13] Ethan Cho: Good context. Do you expect growth and what qps do you need?
[01:18] Rachel Lee: We need 100 qps steady during daytime peaks, occasional bursts to 200 qps. Tail latency for rerank ideally <300ms P95, <200ms median.
[01:29] Tom Watkins: Also cost is a big concern. Storage and per-query vector cost add up.
[01:34] Sofia Martinez: Totally understandable. We typically discuss three deployment options: Hosted API for quick start, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput and lowered per-token/unit costs, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated data. Priya, do you have any redlines for PHI?
[01:48] Priya Srinivasan: Yes. We need HIPAA controls, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and data residency for certain records. We prefer Private or Dedicated inside our VPC if possible.
[01:58] Ethan Cho: Redwood Private supports customer-managed control plane and KMS integration; Dedicated can run in a VPC peered arrangement. For Hosted we have contractual HIPAA add-ons but many customers choose Dedicated/Private for PHI.
[02:09] Rachel Lee: For the rerank model, do you recommend a smaller embedding dimension or keeping 1536? How does that affect throughput/cost?
[02:17] Ethan Cho: There's tradeoffs. 1536 gives better semantic fidelity for some tasks but costs more in storage and compute. We often recommend 768–1024 for production rerank where latency and storage matter; and use a two-stage approach: smaller dims for ANN recall, then a higher-fidelity reranker or cross-encoder on the top K.
[02:33] Sofia Martinez: We can also run prefix caching and KV cache in the runtime to reduce repeated token cost for the reranker step.
[02:40] Tom Watkins: On the vector DB side, we're on Pinecone. If we moved to Redwood's recommended flow, what does integration look like? Can Redwood host vectors or do we keep them in Pinecone?
[02:49] Ethan Cho: Both are options. We integrate with external vector DBs — we can call Pinecone for ANN and take results into Redwood for rerank, or have vectors loaded into our Dedicated infra to reduce cross-network latency. For Private, you'd host vectors locally and Redwood’s runtime can query them over the network. Hybrid search (BM25 + vector rerank) is something we demo often.
[03:07] Rachel Lee: Latency from Pinecone cross-region has bitten us before. If we keep vectors in Pinecone, we'd need a nearby region.
[03:13] Ethan Cho: Yes, network latency matters. For 100 qps with 200ms SLO we'd recommend co-locating or using Dedicated to host embeddings to remove external hops.
[03:22] Priya Srinivasan: For Dedicated/Private, how do you handle keys and auditability? We need to show auditors that KMS keys are customer-controlled and that all inference logs are auditable.
[03:31] Ethan Cho: Dedicated supports bringing-your-own-KMS and we can enable detailed audit logs and retention controls. Private supports HSM integrations for key material. We'll include our SOC2 + HIPAA artifacts.
[03:40] Sofia Martinez: I'll follow up with the security pack.
[03:43] Rachel Lee: Great. On the model side, what's the best pattern for reranking? Cross-encoder vs bi-encoder?
[03:49] Ethan Cho: For high-quality rerank, cross-encoders are better but more expensive per query because they compute pairwise scores. Typical pattern: ANN with dense vectors (bi-encoder) for recall returning top 100, then cross-encoder or cross-attention reranker on top 10-20. That gives strong relevance while controlling cost.
[04:06] Tom Watkins: Can your runtime handle batching for cross-encoder reranks so we amortize token costs?
[04:11] Ethan Cho: Yes, our serving runtime has batching and KV cache. For Dedicated you can tune batch sizes and latency targets. Redwood Optimize will also recommend batch settings based on your query distribution.
[04:21] Rachel Lee: Any recommendations on ANN index type for mixed dims? We have 768 and 1536 vectors.
[04:26] Ethan Cho: Two options: normalize to a single dim by re-embedding older content, or keep two indices and route queries to the appropriate index or upsample with a small model. Many teams standardize to 1024 as a compromise. We can show cost/throughput numbers in the benchmark.
[04:41] Sofia Martinez: Let's talk numbers — for a 100k subset benchmark, what's a typical latency and cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated?
[04:49] Ethan Cho: Rough ballpark: Hosted is fastest to start but per-unit cost higher; Dedicated amortizes GPU and gives 30–60% lower per-query compute cost at scale. For 100 qps sustained with a cross-encoder rerank on top-10, Dedicated can hit P95 ~180–250ms depending on model size and batch tuning. Hosted could meet your latency but costs would be meaningfully higher. We'll produce a concrete estimate in the pricing sheet.
[05:10] Tom Watkins: Can you run benchmarks against our queries?
[05:13] Ethan Cho: Yes — we'll need a sample of anonymized vectors and a set of queries and relevance labels if available. We'll run ANN recall + rerank and provide latency, throughput, and quality metrics (MRR, MAP).
[05:25] Rachel Lee: We can provide anonymized records. We need to check PHI but we'll prepare a dataset.
[05:30] Sofia Martinez: Thanks. Priya, any more security questions before we move to rollout timeline?
[05:35] Priya Srinivasan: A couple: data retention — if we use Hosted can we control retention windows? And does Redwood store raw inputs?
[05:42] Ethan Cho: For Hosted we offer configurable retention and can opt-out of storing raw inputs; for Dedicated and Private, customer data can be isolated and you control retention via your policies. We'll include explicit statements in the security pack.
[05:54] Rachel Lee: Rollout expectations — we'd want a pilot in prod-like environment for 6 weeks, measure relevance and ops impact, then Dedicated reserved capacity if numbers look good. Timeline target: pilot start in June.
[06:06] Sofia Martinez: That aligns. For pilot sizing we'd typically suggest a Dedicated 8-GPU pool for your 100 qps target if you go that route, or Hosted with burst and autoscale for initial pilot.
[06:17] Tom Watkins: What about quantization and model selection? We prefer quantized models if latency/throughput benefits are solid.
[06:22] Ethan Cho: We support quantized inference paths in our runtime and recommend int8/4 quantization for many rerank models with small fidelity loss but big throughput gains. We'll include model/quantization recommendations in the benchmark report.
[06:36] Sofia Martinez: Quick note — customers often use hybrid search: BM25 for keyword recall, ANN for semantic recall, then rerank. Does your team provide tooling to orchestrate that pipeline?
[06:46] Ethan Cho: Yes, Redwood Console and SDK support multi-step pipelines and tracing per-request so you can see which candidates came from BM25 vs ANN and how rerank changed scores. That helps debugging and eval.
[06:57] Rachel Lee: Nice. For evaluation, we need to track regression against our current baseline. Do you support eval sets and automated checks?
[07:03] Ethan Cho: Redwood Optimize and the eval tooling let you bind prompt/test sets and get regression alerts. We can plug your labeled queries if available.
[07:12] Tom Watkins: Any network topology suggestions for Private deployment?
[07:15] Ethan Cho: For Private we recommend colocated infra in your VPC, with peered networks and strict ingress rules. We'll share a network diagram sample.
[07:23] Priya Srinivasan: One more: who has access to logs in Dedicated? We need RBAC and SSO.
[07:29] Ethan Cho: RBAC via SSO (SAML/OIDC) is supported; audit logs can be routed to your SIEM. We'll include default retention and how to configure longer retention.
[07:37] Sofia Martinez: Great. Any competitors you're comparing?
[07:40] Rachel Lee: We're looking at Pinecone + self-hosted cross-encoders and evaluating Milvus for a potential consolidation. Also evaluating managed inference from other vendors.
[07:49] Sofia Martinez: Helpful. We'll call out differences in the security pack and the benchmark doc.
[07:54] Ethan Cho: To make the benchmark useful, we'll run three configs: (1) Hosted Redwood with external Pinecone recall, (2) Dedicated Redwood with vectors co-located and cross-encoder rerank, (3) Private pilot setup in your VPC. We'll measure latency, throughput, MRR, cost per query.
[08:10] Rachel Lee: Sounds good. On cost reporting, can we get token-level and per-route breakdowns?
[08:15] Sofia Martinez: Yes — Console provides token-level cost, per-route, per-model breakdowns and exportable reports.
[08:21] Tom Watkins: Ok. Let's recap next steps quickly.
[08:24] Sofia Martinez: Recap: Redwood sends security docs and Dedicated pricing; SE runs benchmark plan and we schedule a demo focused on hybrid search and rerank results. Customer to provide anonymized dataset and queries. We'll aim to reconvene in one week with initial findings.
[08:40] Rachel Lee: Confirmed. We'll try to get dataset to you by Wednesday.
[08:45] Priya Srinivasan: I'll review the security pack when it arrives.
[08:48] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the shared benchmark sheet.
[08:53] Jorge Alvarez: Thanks all, bye.
[08:55] Tom Watkins: Thanks, bye.
[09:00] (call ends)
